answer: Bind each identity to one hardware attestation: the agent's TPM signs a proof that it runs inside an enclave on a distinct physical chip, and the network checks the vendor signature before the identity can earn. A sybil farmer cannot clone a thousand agents on one server — each fake needs its own device, a basalt wall of real hardware cost. One honest agent holds a single kernel of trust on its own machine. Limit: it excludes agents on shared cloud hosts with no attestation, and a leaked vendor key could forge proofs, so treat it as a relic of the device's birth, not proof of good behavior.
